output.summary: KEP-2784 extends the Certificates API CSR spec with an optional expirationSeconds field so clients can request a specific duration for the issued certificate. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: Certificates issued via the CSR API were not revocable, and clients had no per-CSR way to control certificate duration; built-in signers used one fixed lifespan. The proposal adds a new spec field for clients to request a duration, with signers not required to honor it. The design was accepted, a feature gate was agreed during review so the field could be turned off in a running cluster, and the work was marked implemented on 2022-03-23.

alternatives.option: Add an optional but critical x509 extension to the PEM-encoded CSR in spec.request to carry the desired duration
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this approach offers no benefits over the new field and would make it harder to adopt in the Kubernetes ecosystem.

alternatives.option: Drop the feature gate and enable the behavior unconditionally
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers (deads2k) wanted a gate so that a cluster could turn the behavior off if a controller or approver failed on the field, without rolling back.

alternatives.option: Use an unsigned integer type for the field
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers noted there are no uint examples in the REST API and preferred int32 so negative values can be validated.

evidence.quote: Add a new field to the `spec` of the certificate signing requests API called `expirationSeconds` that allows a client to request a desired duration for the issued certificate.
Requiring signers to honor the requested duration - Configuring existing in-tree consumers of the CSR API (i.e. kubelets) to make use of this feature
Yes. That gives us a way to turn it off in a running cluster without rolling back.
all code, docs, etc for this KEP are complete and it is marked as implemented.
IMO, it is a non-goal but I could see part of the GA requirements being some kind of validation that the kubelet CSR flow could use this
